exam_scheme.note: The Graduate Pharmacy Aptitude Test (GPAT) is the national single-window computer-based entrance examination for admission into Master of Pharmacy (M.Pharm) programmes and for the award of monthly AICTE/PCI postgraduate pharmacy scholarships. Following its transfer from the National Testing Agency (NTA), the examination is conducted by the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS). The examination consists of a single computer-based paper containing 125 multiple-choice questions of 4 marks each, carrying a total of 500 marks, to be answered in 180 minutes (3 hours). The test covers five core subject groups: Pharmaceutical Chemistry & Allied Subjects (38 questions), Pharmaceutics & Allied Subjects (38 questions), Pharmacognosy & Allied Subjects (10 questions), Pharmacology & Allied Subjects (28 questions), and Other Pharmacy Subjects (11 questions). Marking scheme: 4 marks awarded for each correct answer, negative marking of 1 mark deducted for each incorrect answer (-1 mark), and 0 marks for unattempted questions.
